title: Not All Duplicates Are Coordination: Generic vs. Non-Generic Duplicate Campaigns in Information Operations
abstract: arXiv:2609.13671v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Duplicate content is widely used to study coordinated behavior in social media information operations (IOs), but not all repetition provides equally meaningful evidence of coordination. Generic, reusable, or low-information posts may create noisy account-account links when projected into coordination graphs. We study this problem using 187,000 English-language tweets from six Russian Twitter Information Operations datasets. We introduce a generic/non-generic distinction for duplicate campaigns, label tweets using an LLM-assisted protocol with independent human validation, and train supervised classifiers over sentence embeddings to scale the labels. We construct duplicate campaigns using lexical similarity and two embedding-based methods. Generic campaigns are rare under lexical matching but account for nearly 39% of campaigns detected by embedding-based methods. translated_title: 并非所有重复内容都是协同行为：信息作战中的通用与非通用重复活动研究
translated_abstract: 重复内容被广泛用于研究社交媒体信息作战（IO）中的协同行为，但并非所有的重复都能为协同提供同等有意义的证据。通用的、可复用的或低信息量的帖子在投射到协同图时可能会产生嘈杂的账号间连接。我们利用来自六个俄罗斯Twitter信息作战数据集的187,000条英语推文来研究这一问题。我们为重复活动引入了通用/非通用的区分，使用LLM辅助的协议对推文进行标注并进行独立的人工验证，然后在句子嵌入之上训练监督分类器以扩展标注规模。我们使用词汇相似性和两种基于嵌入的方法构建重复活动。在词汇匹配下通用活动较为罕见，但在基于嵌入方法检测到的活动中却占近39%。将协同图限制为非通用活动可以减小图的规模并降低……
tldr: 该研究提出区分“通用”与“非通用”重复活动的新方法，发现基于嵌入方法检测到的信息作战重复活动中近39%为通用低信息量内容，过滤这些内容可显著净化账号协同检测图谱。
